title: Mixed-precision rollout checklist and probe-anchored rollback
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary:

This playbook prescribes an operational checklist and automated rollback heuristics for mixed-precision (mixed-pt/FP16/INT8) rollouts in production. It is intended for model owner engineers, SREs, and the evaluation team. The aim is to reduce unit-costs via lower-precision kernels while bounding customer-visible quality regressions and providing a fast, probe-anchored rollback path when quality or safety thresholds are exceeded.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to model promotion paths where a quantized or mixed-precision variant is introduced into a traffic lane that serves production workloads (hosted, dedicated, or private).
- Covers: pre-rollout evals, live shadowing, canary traffic schedule, probe selection, metric thresholds, automation runbooks, and post-rollout verification.
- Not in scope: model training, architecture changes, or hardware procurement. Those are handled by model-onboarding and infra teams respectively.

Definitions and key signals:
- Probe: a short, labeled input example or seed used to detect regressions (can be deterministic or sampled from live traffic).
- Anchor probes: a small set (~50–200) curated to be highly sensitive to changes known to occur under quantization (e.g., numeric constants, math-heavy reasoning, multi-turn stateful prompts).
- Field probes: sampled live-scenario probes that represent production traffic slices (latency-sensitive, billing-critical, or high-safety).
- Fidelity delta: primary quality metric comparing baseline (FP32 or current prod model) and candidate responses (examples: BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore for generation tasks, top-k accuracy or accept-rate for classification/rerank tasks).
- Response Stability Index (RSI): internal composite that measures structural variance across seeds (0.0–1.0, lower is better).

Rollout checklist (preconditions - must pass all):
1) Offline acceptance: candidate quant-profile has passed the quant-eval gate with these minimum checks:
   - Evaluation suite: all anchor probes executed; mean fidelity delta <= 0.8% (or task-defined guardrail).
   - Coherence check: RSI delta <= 0.015 against baseline.
   - Latency/cost: per-token median latency within configured SLO and expected unit-cost reduction >= 12%.
2) Shadow run: 48–72 hours of shadow traffic with probe telemetry recorded, including prefix/cache warmup.
3) Telemetry gating: at end of shadow run, the following must hold for targeted tenant cohorts:
   - Regression rate on field probes <= 0.5% absolute increase vs baseline.
   - Error-rate (exceptions/timeout) increase <= 0.1% absolute.
4) Canary plan documented and scheduled in the release calendar; automation playbooks created for rollback.
5) Owner and oncall roster assigned; escalation contacts published.

Probe-anchored rollback heuristics (automated):
- High-level policy: execute automated rollback if any of the following probe-derived conditions are met during canary or gradual rollout windows. Each condition is evaluated over a sliding 15-minute window unless stated otherwise.
  1) Fidelity regression breach: aggregate fidelity delta across anchor probes exceeds 2.0% (absolute) for two consecutive windows.
  2) RSI surge: RSI increases by >0.05 relative to baseline and stays above threshold for 30 minutes.
  3) Safety sentinel match-rate: any safety sentinel hits above configured sentinel-threshold for the tenant slice (see table).
  4) Latency tail deterioration: p99 latency degrades by >50% from baseline for the model variant while error-rate >0.05%.
- Escalation priority: automated rollback -> pager to model-owner -> optional hold for manual patch and shadow re-run.

Sampling and probe selection guidance:
- Anchor probes: curated set (50–200) per model family maintained in the probe registry. Update frequency: quarterly or after major model changes.
- Field probes: probabilistic sampling of live requests with stratified sampling by tenant, route, and token-length bucket; sample budget: 0.2% of live requests or 1000 requests/day per tenant, whichever is smaller.
- Probe weighting: anchor probes have weight 3x field probes when computing composite fidelity score to ensure sensitivity to known failure modes.

Metric thresholds and configuration table:

| Signal                         | Canary Threshold             | Gradual rollout threshold | Notes |
|--------------------------------|-----------------------------|---------------------------|-------|
| Aggregate fidelity delta       | > 2.0% (15m window)         | > 1.0% (1h window)        | Use task-specific metric (BLEU/accept-rate) |
| RSI (Response Stability Index) | > 0.05 absolute             | > 0.03 absolute           | RSI is normalized per model family |
| Safety sentinel hit-rate       | > 0.1% of probe hits        | > 0.05% of probe hits     | Per-tenant safety guardrails can be stricter |
| Error-rate (exceptions)        | > 0.5%                      | > 0.2%                    | Includes timeouts and invalid responses |
| p99 latency change             | > +50%                      | > +25%                    | Measured on the serving variant at the same token budget |

Operational runbook (step-by-step):
1) Initiate canary: start with 1% traffic for 2 hours. Ensure probe telemetry is tagged with rollout_id and cohort.
2) Monitor automated gates (dashboard + alerts): fidelity_delta_alert, rsi_alert, sentinel_rate_alert, latency_tail_alert.
3) If any automated gate fires:
   a) Immediately flip traffic back to baseline (automation).
   b) Alert model-owner and SRE via pager (pager duty runbook id: PD-quant-rollout).
   c) Capture snapshot: model variant artifact, quantization profile, kernel selection, and a 15-minute telemetry dump to the incident bucket.
   d) Run adaptive bisect: if traffic change was incremental (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 10%), use rollout-bisect to identify the smallest cohort where probe failures started.
4) If gates do not fire after 6 hours at 1%: progress to 5% for 4 hours, then 10% for 4 hours, then follow the scheduled ramp to target.
5) Post-rollout verification: after reaching target, run the post-rollout probe sweep (all anchor probes + 5k field probes) and store verification report in the model artifact registry.

Automation snippets (examples):
- Sample manifest (rollout manifest consumed by the release agent):

{
  "rollout_id": "mp-rollout-2025-03-10-01",
  "model_baseline": "decoder-v3-fp32@2025-02-28",
  "candidate": "decoder-v3-mp-int8@2025-03-10",
  "probe_sets": ["anchor:decoder-v3-anch-2025-01", "field:tenant-sampled-2025-03-09"],
  "initial_traffic_pct": "1",
  "ramp_plan": "1->5->10->25->50->100",
  "rollback_policy": "probe-anchored-v1"
}

- CLI: start a canary (release agent):
$ rwald rollout start --manifest rollout_mp.json --env prod --notify-on-rollbacks

- Automation policy example (pseudo-YAML used by release controller):
rollout_policy: |
  name: probe-anchored-v1
  evaluate_every: 15m
  failure_conditions:
    - metric: fidelity_delta
      comparator: gt
      value: 2.0
      window: 15m
    - metric: rsi_delta
      comparator: gt
      value: 0.05
      window: 30m
  actions:
    - on_failure: rollback_automated
    - on_failure: notify(model_owner)

Practical notes and known failure modes:
- Cache/kv-warmup differences can hide quantization regressions in short shadow runs. Always include a warmup period equivalent to median session length.
- Mixed-precision kernels can change latency characteristics non-linearly depending on sequence length buckets; monitor per-token-latency histograms per bucket.
- Some safety-sensitive prompts flip from benign to risky only with small token-level changes — such cases are best covered by targeted anchor probes and safety sentinels.

Post-rollback investigation checklist:
- Reproduce locally with the same quant profile and kernel selection. Capture full operator logs.
- Run a focused probe sweep around the failing anchors + 2x neighboring probes.
- If failure is workload-sensitive (tenant-specific), collect representative session traces and escalate to tenant-ops.
- If a kernel-level performance regression suspected, engage serving-runtime team (pager: runtime-kernel-investigation).

Ownership and contacts:
- Model Owner: team lead or listed owner in the model registry (ensure model artifact has owner tag).
- SRE contact: eng-sre/quant-rollout rotation.
- Eval & QA: Applied ML evaluations team (eva-team@redwood.ai).

Revision history and maintenance cadence:
- Playbook owner must review quarterly and after any production rollback caused by quantization.
- Anchor probe sets are refreshed quarterly; field probe sampling budget reviewed monthly.

Related artifacts and references:
- See model artifact registry for the candidate and baseline model descriptors.
- Related runbooks: quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026, quantized-artifact-eval-gate-and-rollout-2026.

Attachments and templates (copy to use):
- Rollout manifest template: rollout_mp.json (example above).
- Post-rollout verification checklist (spreadsheet template in team drive).

If you are running the first rollout for a model family, open a rollout readiness ticket and schedule a 30-minute readiness review with SRE and applied-ml-evals.
notes: This document is a synthesized operational playbook combining quantization-profile guidance, eval probe policy, and SRE automation steps. Tailor thresholds per-model family and task domain before use.
